program.name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
program.description:
Supplemental Security Income (SSI) gives monthly cash payments. It helps older adults and people who are blind or have a disability.

Your monthly payment depends on your income, living situation, and other factors. You can use the money for food, clothing, housing, and other basic needs.

SSI has a resource limit. Resources include cash and money in bank accounts. Some things you own do not count. Social Security checks your resources when you apply. Living in some institutions may also affect your SSI payment.

Click 'Apply Now' to start your SSI application with Social Security. You can also apply by phone by calling 1-800-772-1213.

program.website_description: Monthly cash help for older adults and people who are blind or have a disability

warning_messages.message: If you get SSDI, the amount of your SSI payment may be lower. In some cases, you may not get SSI if you also get SSDI.
If you apply based on a disability, the first decision usually takes 6 to 8 months. If Social Security denies your application, you can appeal the decision.

documents.text: Proof of identity, if requested (such as a driver's license or state ID)
Proof of age (birth certificate or other birth record)
Lease, rent receipt, and household cost information
Proof of work income (pay stubs or tax return)
Proof of other income (award letters, bank statements, or court orders)
Proof of citizenship or immigration status
Bank statements and records of property or other resources
Medical records, provider contacts, and medicines (for disability or blindness claims)
School records or IEP (for child disability claims)

navigators.name: The Whole Person
navigators.description: The Whole Person helps people with disabilities apply for SSI or SSDI. Staff can help gather documents, communicate with Social Security, and prepare appeals.
